explanation: The hypothesis captures the broad, scientifically credible idea that selective Al oxidation can create a slow-growing external alumina scale above 900 °C. Its controlled Al-versus-no-Al experiment and explicit falsification rule are reasonably discriminating. However, it does not closely reconstruct the target study: the actual intervention was temperature-resolved heating to 1100 °C under air and low-p(O2)/vacuum, with oxygen availability governing scale thickness and Al consumption. The target mechanism also involved outward Al and secondary Cr diffusion, an outer Al2O3/inner Cr2O3-rich duplex scale, Al-depleted subsurface phase transformation, and temperature-dependent FCC/sigma evolution. The generated prediction instead assumes that Al alone produces a coherent, adherent scale and that Al-free material necessarily cracks or spalls, neither of which was demonstrated by the target results. Its 50–100 hour isothermal conditions, single-phase restriction, compositional baseline, and omission of the BCC/B2-to-FCC/sigma transformations substantially reduce condition and outcome agreement.
